title: Add a candidate Table I task and penalty reward
summary: locomotion.paper_reward implements the task-tracking and penalty terms of Liu et al. Table I on this robot's telemetry, beside the unchanged task.measured_reward. It restores the missing minus sign in the tracking exponent, derives joint acceleration from consecutive controls, approximates the collision count by non-foot ground contact above 1 N, and applies the torque limit to requested torque against the 1.6 N·m cap. It omits the style term and the foot contact-force limit. A separate paper_reward_calibrated variant rescales the five continuous penalties so that, on seven recorded focus-case rollouts, they together average 0.8 of the mean tracking reward in equal shares; the limit and collision terms keep the printed weights. python -m locomotion.paper_reward reproduces the calibration from the traces recorded by SHA-256. The scorer and viewer score either variant with --reward and now supply previous joint velocity, raw and previous actions and requested torque from control traces.
next: Publish a score report comparing the candidate with the current reward on the paired PPO and optimizer replay traces, including each reward's motionless counterfactual, before proposing it for training.
reason: A candidate reward scored offline changes no measured result, roadmap marker, gate or the training reward in locomotion/task.py.
